instructions: Scrub the 1 1/4 lbs sweet potatoes but leave the skin on. Cut them diagonally into bite-size pieces, turning the potato a quarter turn between cuts.
Stir the 2 tsp salt into 8 cups of water in a large bowl. Add the potato pieces and soak for 15 minutes.
Drain the potatoes and pat them very dry with a clean towel.
Pour the 2 cups oil into a medium pot and heat it over medium heat to 320°F. No thermometer? Dip the end of a wooden chopstick in the oil: small, steady bubbles should rise around it.
Add half the potatoes and fry for 5 to 7 minutes, until golden brown. A skewer should slide in easily. Transfer them to a wire rack or paper towels. Repeat with the rest.
In a large frying pan, off the heat, mix the 5 tbsp sugar, 1 1/2 tbsp water and 1 tbsp mirin. Put it on medium heat and bring it to a boil.

Once it's bubbling, stir in the 1 tsp rice vinegar and 1 tsp soy sauce. Simmer for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring constantly, until the syrup thickens. It's ready when a line drawn across the pan with your spatula holds its shape.
Turn off the heat, add all the fried potatoes and toss until each piece is coated. Sprinkle the 1 tsp sesame seeds over the top while the coating is still soft.
Spread them out and leave for a few minutes. The coating hardens as it cools. Serve warm or at room temperature. Let them cool completely before packing them in a lunchbox.
method_notes: Just One Cookbook soaks the cut potato in salted water, fries at 320°F and tosses it in a sugar, water and mirin syrup finished with rice vinegar and soy. RecipeTin Japan fries twice (320°F then 356°F) in a honey or sugar syrup, and No Recipes steams the potato first and glazes with rice syrup, so this follows the first. Just One Cookbook also has a shallow fry version, which was not used because the deep fry gives the crunchy outside. Frying time per batch is an estimate, so use the skewer test. RecipeTin Japan shows 2 ratings and No Recipes 3.
